module_role: Source-synchronous parallel memory device intended to be paired with a DDR3 memory controller + PHY. JESD79-3C standardizes the SDRAM component side (ball assignment, electrical signaling, command/address protocol, mode registers, AC timing). The controller / PHY side is OUT of scope of this spec but must implement: (a) clock + DQS generation, (b) command scheduler honouring tRCD/tRP/tRAS/tRC/tRRD/tFAW/tWR/tWTR/tCCD/tRFC/tREFI/tMRD/tMOD/tXP/tXPDLL/tXS/tXSDLL/tZQ*, (c) ZQ calibration, (d) Write Leveling, (e) Read training (MPR), (f) per-bank state tracking. Concrete DDR3 controller IP appears in CPU SoCs, FPGA hard cores (Xilinx MIG, Intel UniPHY), and SoC IP vendors (Synopsys DesignWare DDR3, Cadence Denali).

integration_overview.wire_directions: CK/CK#, CKE, CS#, ODT, RAS#/CAS#/WE#, BA[2:0], A[15:0], DM, RESET#: controller → DRAM (input only). DQ, DQS/DQS#: bidirectional. TDQS/TDQS#: DRAM → controller (output only, x8 only). ZQ: tied to ground via 240 Ω. VREFDQ, VREFCA: input reference voltages.
integration_overview.rank_selection: CS# is the rank-level chip select on multi-rank DIMMs; ODT is per-rank.
integration_overview.no_handshake: Deterministic latency; data transfer follows the command without per-beat acknowledgment.
integration_overview.DIMM_routing: Standard DDR3 UDIMM/SODIMM uses fly-by command/address/control topology (instead of DDR2 T-branch); per-DRAM flight-time skew between CK and DQS is compensated by the controller via Write Leveling.

interconnect_topologies_supported: Single controller + single DRAM component (point-to-point on FPGA / SoC boards).
Single controller + DDR3 UDIMM (Unbuffered DIMM): fly-by command/address/control to multiple DRAMs on the module, per-DRAM DQ groups.
Single controller + DDR3 SO-DIMM (notebook form factor): same fly-by topology, half-size board.
Single controller + DDR3 RDIMM (Registered DIMM): registered command/address (extra register chip latches CA before fanout to DRAMs).
Single controller + DDR3 LRDIMM (Load-Reduced DIMM): buffered command/address AND buffered DQ via memory buffer chip; supports higher rank counts.
Multi-rank DIMMs (CS0#, CS1#, ODT0, ODT1 per rank): up to 8 ranks via 3-bit CS encoding (rare in DDR3).
default_signal_values_when_omitted: On a DDR3 UDIMM the on-board terminator chips clamp inputs to known levels during reset. CKE has a 0.2 × VDD effective pull-down at the DRAM input until the controller drives it. RESET# is the only asynchronous control; it must be deliberately driven HIGH by the controller before normal operation.
soc_dependent_items: DDR3 controller / scheduler IP (vendor IP — Synopsys DDR3 PHY, Cadence Denali, Xilinx MIG, Intel UniPHY, OpenSource LiteDRAM).
DLL / DQS phase-locking PHY (1 PHY per byte lane; deskew + RX FIFO + per-bit deskew on UHS designs).
ZQ calibration sequencer (issues ZQCS periodically; tracks Tdrift / Vdrift).
Write Leveling sequencer (sweeps DQS-to-CK delay during init and after major Vdd/temp changes).
Per-bank state tracker (open row + tRAS / tRC bookkeeping per bank).
Refresh scheduler (tREFI tracking with up to 8 postponed/pulled-in REFs).
VDD / VDDQ regulator (1.5 V or 1.35 V or 1.25 V).
VREF generator (VDD/2 + VDDQ/2 references with low noise).
RESET# generation (board-level reset combined with controller's PHY reset).
Optional ECC encoder/decoder for system-level data protection (SEC-DED on x8 byte lanes by adding an extra ×8 ECC DRAM).

pull_up_resistors_terminators.termination: Differential ODT at end-of-line on DIMM (typically 100 Ω parallel between CK and CK#).
Fly-by VTT termination resistors (typ. 39 Ω to VTT = VDD/2) at end of CA bus on DIMM.
On-die termination (ODT) controlled by Rtt_Nom (MR1) + Rtt_WR (MR2) per the system topology. External VTT termination not used (DDR3 relies on ODT).
Controller-driven push-pull; no termination required, but board pull-up to VDD typical.
240 Ω ±1% to ground per DRAM (or shared between two DRAMs if calibration windows do not overlap).

low_power_modes.Active_Power_Down: CKE LOW with one or more banks open; tXP to exit. DLL stays on. Lower IDD but rapid return to operation.
low_power_modes.Precharge_Power_Down_Fast_Exit: CKE LOW with all banks precharged, MR0 A12=1 (DLL on). tXP exit.
low_power_modes.Precharge_Power_Down_Slow_Exit: CKE LOW with all banks precharged, MR0 A12=0 (DLL frozen). tXPDLL exit. Lower IDD but slower wake.
low_power_modes.Self_Refresh: Deepest mode: CKE LOW with SRE; DRAM generates internal refresh; external CK may be stopped; VDD must remain valid. Exit via CKE rising + tCKSRX + tXS/tXSDLL.
low_power_modes.Deep_Power_Down: Not a defined DDR3 state at the protocol level — DDR3 has no DPD command. To fully power down: stop CK, drive CKE LOW, drive RESET# LOW; VDD/VDDQ removal possible only after RESET# is LOW. Re-init required after VDD return.

compatibility_notes: DDR3 is NOT pin-compatible nor protocol-compatible with DDR2: different signaling (SSTL_15 vs SSTL_18), different ballout, different reset (RESET# pin), different burst architecture (8n vs 4n prefetch), different mode register layout, and different topology (fly-by vs T-branch on DIMM).
DDR3L (1.35 V) and DDR3U (1.25 V) DRAMs are protocol-compatible with DDR3 but at reduced VDD. Mixed-voltage operation requires the controller PHY to drive at the lower of the supported voltages.
DDR3 RDIMM / LRDIMM add a register / memory-buffer chip that introduces additional latency (CA registered → +1 cycle CA-to-DRAM); the controller must adjust tRCD bookkeeping accordingly.
x4, x8, x16 DRAMs share the same protocol and command set but differ in DQ width, DM / TDQS behaviour, and column address bit count.
